sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow

instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_ollama-gemma4-31b_01.html`.

{"edit_description":"Implement the `step()` method in the `Chip8` class to decode and execute a single instruction. 
Implement the complete set of 35 CHIP-8 instructions. 
Group them logically:
1. Control Flow: 00EE (Return), 1NNN (Jump), 2NNN (Call), AXXX (Skip if V[X]==0), CXXX (Skip if V[X]!=0).
2. Memory/Index: 6XXX (Set V[X]), 7XXX (Add to V[X]), 8XXX (Arithmetic/Logic: ADD, SUB, XOR, OR, AND, SHIFT), 9XXX (Set V[X] if V[X]!=0), AXXX (Set I), BX XX (Set I to address with V[X]), EXXX (Equate/Save/Load: EX40, EX41, EXA1).
3. Display/Input: DXYN (Draw Sprite), FXXX (Wait for Key), GXXX (Read Key).
4. Miscellaneous: 00VD (Clear Display), 00VN (Set V[N] to I), 00VV (Set V[V] to V[V] - though usually 00VV is not standard, check 00VV vs 00VD), 00XN (Set PC to NN), 00XN (Set I to NN), etc.

Ensure that:
- The 8-bit arithmetic overflow/underflow is handled correctly in VF.
- The shift instructions (8XY6, 8XY7) behave according to the standard (either shift V[X] or shift V[Y] into V[X]).
- BCD conversion (FX33) is implemented.
- XOR sprite drawing is handled by a separate method `drawSprite(x, y, height, spriteData)` which we will refine in the next step, but the opcode DXYN should call it.

Add a `decodeInstruction(opcode)` method that returns a human-readable string of the current instruction for the debugger.

Replace the script content to include these methods within the `Chip8` class.","path":"chip8_ollama-gemma4-31b_01.html"}
